audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and phases[].side disagreed with the whys at levels 1, 2, 3, 4-5 and 6.
audit.why: Before Quickdraw, Gwen's cone contests the first wave; with Quickdraw plus Smoke Screen he owns 2 and 3; 4-5 is described as even; and at 6 Hallowed Mist plus Needlework force a short-range shotgun to fight where he cannot target her. All five are stated in the existing prose.
audit.corrected: Gwen / Graves / Graves / Skill / Gwen / Gwen / Gwen.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns despite the page telling you twice to play around Smoke Screen and Quickdraw.
audit.why: Smoke Screen is 26/24/22/20/18, Quickdraw 16/15/14/13/12, End of the Line 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6 and Collateral Damage 100/80/60. Smoke Screen at 26s is longer than your 22s Hallowed Mist, which means after he spends it you have a mist cycle he cannot answer - that is the actual shape of the window.
audit.corrected: mid, whys[3] and wants.you[2] now carry the numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says his pellets 'land outside the fog' when you mist, which slightly overstates what Hallowed Mist does.
audit.why: Riot's text: Gwen can only be targeted by enemies who enter the mist. That stops him TARGETING you from outside, but End of the Line and Collateral Damage are skillshot projectiles that still travel and still connect - the mist beats his autos and pellets, not his Q or R. Telling a player the fog eats everything is how they die to a Collateral Damage they thought was blocked.
audit.corrected: mid now distinguishes his targeted pellets from his skillshots.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are even but tense — he still kites with Quickdraw and slows you with Smoke Screen, but your Q+E poke-and-reset lets you trade back when his shells are reloading, so it comes down to who plays the dash-and-slow windows better. At 6 the lane flips to you: drop Hallowed Mist as he Quickdraws in so his pellets land outside the fog, slow him with Needlework, and make him fight a short-range shotgun in a zone where he can't target you. Bait out his Smoke Screen and let his shells reload before you commit your E autos, not after.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are even but tense — he kites with Quickdraw and slows you with Smoke Screen, but your Q+E poke-and-reset trades back while his shells reload. Smoke Screen is 26s at rank 1, longer than your 22s Mist, so once he spends it you get a full mist cycle he cannot answer. At 6 the lane flips to you: drop Hallowed Mist as he Quickdraws in so his pellets cannot target you, slow him with Needlework, and make a short-range shotgun fight inside the fog. The fog stops his autos, not his skillshots — End of the Line and Collateral Damage still travel.

edits.before: Once your first AP item lands (Riftmaker or Nashor's into the Blackfire line) you own the extended fight — Skip 'n Slash's cooldown refund keeps your on-hit autos and %-HP Q rolling while his tanky-ADC build just feeds your Thousand Cuts passive more max-HP to shred and more healing to sustain on. He's a burst-and-disengage threat, so the danger is never the straight 1v1 — it's him Quickdrawing out of your mist and re-engaging once it's off cooldown. Pin him in fog, slow with R, and don't chase a Graves who's already dashed and slowed you; let him come back into your mist.
edits.after: Once your first AP item lands (Riftmaker or Nashor's into the Blackfire line) you own the extended fight — Skip 'n Slash's cooldown refund keeps your on-hit autos and %-HP Q rolling while his tanky-ADC build just feeds A Thousand Cuts more max-HP to shred and more healing to sustain on. He is a burst-and-disengage threat, so the danger is never the straight 1v1 — it is him Quickdrawing out of your mist and re-engaging on a 16s cooldown. Pin him in fog, slow with R, and do not chase a Graves who has already dashed; let him come back into your mist.

edits.after: Even window — your Q+E poke-and-reset trades back while his shells reload, and a spent 26s Smoke Screen is your opening, but his slow-and-kite still answers it.

edits.before: You out-scale his pellets the more he builds HP — your Thousand Cuts passive shreds his max-HP and heals you off it, so pin him in mist and the extended duel is yours.
edits.after: You out-scale his pellets the more he builds HP — A Thousand Cuts shreds his max-HP and heals you off it, so pin him in mist and the extended duel is yours.

notes: Names correct, prose second-person, and the level-6 mist play is well explained. Fixes: (1) the chart contradicted the prose at five of seven stages - whys[0] says you contest level 1 before Quickdraw exists, whys[1] and whys[2] give him 2 and 3, whys[3] calls 4-5 even, whys[4] says 6 flips to you. Set to Gwen/Graves/Graves/Skill/Gwen/Gwen/Gwen. I did not take the packet's 'Graves at 6', because whys[4] and spikes[2] both say level 6 is the flip. (2) The page says 'bait out his Smoke Screen' without the number: it is 26s at rank 1, the longest cooldown in his kit and longer than your 22s Hallowed Mist, so a spent Smoke Screen is a real window rather than a hope. (3) 'Thousand Cuts' was missing its 'A' in three places. NOT VERIFIED: the page credits Quickdraw with 'True Grit armor'. Riot's kit data for Quickdraw in champ-data only carries the dash flag and says nothing about armour, so I left that clause untouched rather than assert or delete it.
